items.title: Binary adjacency matrix of an ordered finite simple graph
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with a fixed order
$V=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$. Put $\mathbb F_2:=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$; the
field law follows from [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]] at $p=2$, and this field has
order two by [[def-finite-field-and-its-order]]. Define the binary adjacency
matrix $A_2(G)\in M_n(\mathbb F_2)$ by

$$ (A_2(G))_{jk}=\begin{cases}1,&\{v_j,v_k\}\in E,\\0,&\{v_j,v_k\}\notin E.\end{cases} $$

The indices use the ordered bit coordinates of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. Since edges are unordered pairs of
distinct vertices, $A_2(G)$ is symmetric and has zero diagonal. This is a
matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, using [[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]];
it is not the root library's real-valued adjacency matrix. When $V=\varnothing$,
$A_2(G)$ is the unique $0\times0$ matrix.

references.title: Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096

proof_obligations: define vertex-order dependence and arithmetic mod 2; do not depend on the real-valued root adjacency matrix.

items.title: J gate and ordered equatorial measurement vectors
items.statement:
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, let
$P_\alpha=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\alpha})$ and
$J(\alpha)=H P_\alpha$, with $H$ and the exact one-qubit gate convention
from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. Define the ordered
measurement vectors

$$ |b\rangle_\alpha:=J(\alpha)^\dagger|b\rangle,\qquad b\in\{0,1\}, $$

where $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ are the ordered computational basis vectors.
The adjoint and complex inner product use the root convention translated by
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The global phase in $J(\alpha)$
is fixed by the displayed matrix product; it is not suppressed.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §20.6
Robert Raussendorf and Hans J. Briegel, Quantum computing via measurements only, arXiv:quant-ph/0010033

items.title: J-gate basis and exact phase identities
items.statement:
For every $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, $J(\alpha)$ is unitary and
$\{|0\rangle_\alpha,|1\rangle_\alpha\}$ is an orthonormal basis. The exact
identities

$$ J(0)=H,\qquad J(0)^2=I,\qquad J(-\beta)X=e^{-i\beta}ZJ(\beta),\qquad J(\pi/2)^3=e^{i\pi/4}I $$

hold in the fixed phase convention.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: Verify unitarity and basis orthonormality from the exact matrices; multiply both sides of the phase identity; compute the three-J scalar exactly.

items.title: Graph state of an ordered finite simple graph
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with a fixed vertex order. Let
$\mathcal H_V=\bigotimes_{v\in V}\mathbb C^2$ use that order and its ordered
computational basis, as in [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]],
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], and
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For each edge $\{u,v\}$ let
$CZ_{uv}$ be the unique full-register local embedding from
[[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]] of the controlled phase gate with angle
$\pi$ from [[def-qc-controlled-phase-rotation]]. Order the endpoints so that
$u$ precedes $v$ in the fixed vertex order; the embedded two-qubit matrix is
$\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,-1)$ in the ordered pair basis
$|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, and every other tensor factor
acts as the identity. Thus the two local factors have the same order as the
edge endpoints, within the full register ordered by $V$. Order the finite edge
set lexicographically by its ordered endpoint indices and define

$$ |G\rangle:=\left(\prod_{\{u,v\}\in E}^{\mathrm{lex}}CZ_{uv}\right)|+\rangle^{\otimes V},\qquad |+\rangle=2^{-1/2}(|0\rangle+|1\rangle). $$

The lexicographic order makes the product a specified finite composition.
If $V=\varnothing$, the tensor product and empty product act on the
one-dimensional trivial register and $|G\rangle$ is its unit vector.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: establish incident edge gates commute, so the finite product is order-independent.

items.title: Controlled-Z matching action on a Pauli frame
items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and let $M$ be a matching, meaning a set of pairwise disjoint
two-element subsets of the ordered wire set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Give the graph
$G_M=(\{1,\ldots,n\},M)$ the vertex order $1,\ldots,n$, so vertex $j$ is
coordinate $j$ (position $j-1$ in the zero-based vertex list) of its binary
adjacency matrix. Let $A_M:=A_2(G_M)\in M_n(\mathbb F_2)$ from
[[def-qc-binary-adjacency-matrix]], so $(A_M)_{jk}=1$ exactly when
$\{j,k\}\in M$. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, all coordinates use this wire
order, and binary dot products mean $a\cdot b:=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jb_j$ in
$\mathbb F_2$. Define $q_M(x):=\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M}x_jx_k\in\mathbb F_2$.
For $n\ge1$, put
$P(x,z):=X^xZ^z=P(0,x,z)$ as in
[[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]]. For $n=0$, the unique empty
vectors satisfy $X^x=Z^z=I_{\mathbb C}$ and we define $P(x,z)=I_{\mathbb C}$;
the register is the empty tensor product from
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. With
$CZ_M:=\prod_{\{j,k\}\in M}CZ_{jk}$,

$$CZ_M P(x,z)=(-1)^{q_M(x)}P(x,z\oplus A_Mx)CZ_M.$$

For the empty wire set or empty matching the sum is zero and the formula is
the identity.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §20.6
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, §II B

proof_obligations: Expand the matching quadratic form on computational basis vectors and retain the sign when both endpoints have X support.

items.title: Normalized transport schedule for a J/CZ circuit
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a finite $n$-wire circuit over the $J(\alpha)$ and $CZ$ gates, with chronological layers
$L_1,\ldots,L_d$ and source wire labels $0,\ldots,n-1$ as in
[[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. Schedule index $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$
denotes source wire $j-1$. For each source layer $L_r$, let $M_r$ be the
matching of its $CZ$ occurrences after reindexing a source pair $\{u,v\}$ as
$\{u+1,v+1\}$, and let $J_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be the indices carrying
one-qubit gates $J(\alpha_{rj})$. The source layer has pairwise disjoint gate
supports by [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], so no $J$ gate in
$J_r$ meets an edge of $M_r$. By
[[lem-qc-disjoint-layer-order-independence]], its denotation may be written
with the CZ matching first and then at most one $J(\alpha_{rj})$ per schedule
index $j$. The
**normalized transport schedule** $\mathcal T(C)$ is the finite chronological
list of rounds $(M_s,(\alpha_{s1},\ldots,\alpha_{sn}))$ and the scalar
$\sigma_C$ defined as follows. A round applies its matching first and then
one $J$ gate on each wire. Define
$\sigma_C=\prod_{r:0<|J_r|<n}e^{i\pi(n-|J_r|)/4}$. The round list is the
concatenation, in source-layer order, of the blocks specified by the first
matching case below; the empty product is $1$. This order makes the
zero-wire empty-layer case unambiguous:

1. If $J_r=\varnothing$ and $M_r=\varnothing$, the block is empty.
2. If $n\ge1$ and $J_r=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the block consists of one round with matching
   $M_r$ and the original angles $\alpha_{rj}$.
3. If $J_r=\varnothing$ and $M_r\ne\varnothing$, the block consists of two rounds: the
   first has matching $M_r$ and angle $0$ on every wire; the second has no
   matching and angle $0$ on every wire.
4. If $0<|J_r|<n$, the block consists of three rounds. The first has matching $M_r$,
   angle $\alpha_{rj}$ on active wires $j\in J_r$, and angle $\pi/2$ on
   idle wires. The next two have no matching, angle $0$ on active wires,
   and angle $\pi/2$ on idle wires. The factor for this mixed layer is
   included in the displayed product defining $\sigma_C$.

The rounds are numbered $s=1,\ldots,R$ in concatenation order. Their schedule
indices continue to denote the corresponding source wires $j-1$. Angles at
indices without an original $J$ gate are padding angles. For a mixed layer,
the active-wire product is $J(0)J(0)J(\alpha)=J(\alpha)$ and each idle wire
contributes $J(\pi/2)^3=e^{i\pi/4}I$; the scalar is therefore recorded in
$\sigma_C$ rather than suppressed. The no-$J$ matching case has two
$J(0)=H$ transports, whose product is $I$. No claim about the transport
graph's simplicity is part of this definition.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §20.6
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, §§II D–F

proof_obligations: State the layer order and handle empty, fully occupied, CZ-only, and mixed layers.
Retain the scalar from each mixed layer and bound R by 3d.

items.title: One-bit J-gate teleportation branch identity
items.statement:
For a normalized qubit $|\psi\rangle=a|0\rangle+c|1\rangle$ and real
$\alpha$, prepare $CZ(|\psi\rangle\otimes|+\rangle)$ and project the first
qubit in the ordered basis $\{|b\rangle_\alpha:b=0,1\}$ of
[[def-qc-j-gate-and-equatorial-basis]]. The outcome-$b$ branch operator on the
second qubit is

$$K_b=2^{-1/2}X^bJ(\alpha).$$

Thus each outcome has probability $1/2$ and the normalized output is
$X^bJ(\alpha)|\psi\rangle$. The operator identity is linear and therefore
also holds when the input qubit is entangled with a finite-dimensional
reference register.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf and Hans J. Briegel, Quantum computing via measurements only, arXiv:quant-ph/0010033
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: expand amplitudes and check each branch norm.

items.title: Exact Gray-code synthesis of multiplexed y- and z-axis rotations
items.statement:
For $k\ge0$ controls and real angles $\theta_x$ indexed by
$x\in\{0,1\}^k$, let
$$M_a=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_a(\theta_x), \qquad a\in\{y,z\},$$
where $R_y(\theta)=R_{(0,1,0)}(\theta)$ and
$R_z(\theta)=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta)$ use the exact exponential convention of
[[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. There is an exact finite
circuit for $M_a$ on the same $k+1$ wires, using arbitrary one-qubit
rotations and CNOT gates and no ancillas. For $k=0$ it is one rotation and no
CNOT; for $k>0$ it uses $2^k$ target rotations and $2^k$ CNOTs. The circuit
uses exact real angle labels; no finite-bit encoding or synthesis-time bound
is asserted.

references.title: Vivek V. Shende, Stephen S. Bullock, and Igor L. Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, arXiv:quant-ph/0406176v5, §§3 and 5
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §2.2

proof_obligations: Prove the cyclic Gray traversal and Walsh inversion exactly.
Verify both rotation signs from the fixed Pauli convention; do not use the QC11 axis-sign mismatch.
Cover k=0 and the final parity-restoring CNOT.

items.title: Computational-basis amplitudes of a graph state
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an ordered finite simple graph with $n=|V|$. In the ordered
computational basis indexed by $x\in\mathbb F_2^V$,

$$ |G\rangle=2^{-n/2}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_2^V}(-1)^{\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}x_ux_v}|x\rangle, $$

where the exponent is evaluated as an integer and only its parity affects the
sign.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096

proof_obligations: multiply edge phases and retain normalization.

items.title: Controlled-Z edge gates commute
items.statement:
For any two edges $e,f$ of a finite simple graph on an ordered qubit register,
the embedded operators $CZ_e$ and $CZ_f$ commute. Consequently the finite
graph-state edge product is independent of the ordering of its edges.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: Use the diagonal computational-basis action, including disjoint edges, edges sharing one vertex, and the empty edge set.

items.title: Finite open-graph adaptive measurement pattern
items.statement:
An **open-graph adaptive measurement pattern** consists of an ordered finite
simple graph $G=(V,E)$, input and output subsets $I,O\subseteq V$, an ordering
$m_1,\ldots,m_q$ of $M:=V\setminus O$, basis-choice functions
$\alpha_j:\{0,1\}^{j-1}\to\mathbb R$, and a terminal correction function
$C:\{0,1\}^q\to U(\mathcal H_O)$. For each subset $S\subseteq V$, write
$\mathcal H_S:=\bigotimes_{v\in S}\mathbb C^2$ in inherited vertex order,
with $\mathcal H_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. The tensor register $\mathcal H_V$
and all wire permutations use the fixed vertex order. Let
$\Pi_{I,V\setminus I}:\mathcal H_V\to
\mathcal H_I\otimes\mathcal H_{V\setminus I}$ be the wire permutation listing
$I$ first and then $V\setminus I$, each in inherited order. Let
$a_+:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C^2$ be the linear map $c\mapsto c|+\rangle$, and
let $a_{+,V\setminus I}:=\bigotimes_{v\in V\setminus I}a_+$ in inherited
order. Using the empty-tensor identifications, define the ordered input map
$$\iota_I:=\Pi_{I,V\setminus I}^{-1} (I_{\mathcal H_I}\otimes a_{+,V\setminus I}): \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_V.$$
Thus the input is unchanged and each complementary vertex receives $|+\rangle$.
Apply $U_G:=\prod_{\{u,v\}\in E}^{\mathrm{lex}}CZ_{uv}$.
At step $j$, after transcript prefix $b_1,\ldots,b_{j-1}$, measure vertex
$m_j$ in the ordered basis $\{|b_j\rangle_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}:b_j\in\{0,1\}\}$
from [[def-qc-j-gate-and-equatorial-basis]]. The measured systems are removed
and the vertices in $O$ are retained in their inherited order.

Let $\Pi_{M,O}$ be the tensor permutation listing $m_1,\ldots,m_q$ first and
the vertices of $O$ in inherited order. For a full transcript
$\mathbf b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)$, define the linear measurement contraction
$$B_{\mathbf b}:= \left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^q {}_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}\!\langle b_j|_{m_j}\right)\otimes I_{\mathcal H_O},$$
where the bras are the linear functionals from
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]], their tensor map is formed in
$m_1,\ldots,m_q$ order, so
$B_{\mathbf b}:\mathcal H_{m_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal H_{m_q}
\otimes\mathcal H_O\to\mathcal H_O$. The scalar output
$\mathbb C^{\otimes q}$ is identified with
$\mathbb C$ by the tensor-unit convention. This tensor map is supplied by
[[def-qc-tensor-map]]; for $q=0$ its measured-register factor is the identity
on the empty tensor product. The branch map is the ordered composition

$$K_{\mathbf b}=B_{\mathbf b}\Pi_{M,O}U_G\iota_I: \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_O.$$

The measured systems are removed and the vertices in $O$ are retained in
their inherited order. This pattern uses $|V|$ qubit registers, its width in
the convention of [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. Its projective
measurement count is $q$, counting one occurrence for each listed vertex
$m_j$. On a normalized pure input its
probability is $\|K_{\mathbf b}\psi\|^2$; for a density operator $\rho$ it is
$\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)$. The conditional
output is normalized only when that probability is positive. The corrected
branch is $C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$; the correction does not change the
branch probability. This is a finite-dimensional mathematical circuit and
instrument semantics, with no physical postulate or implementation claim.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: define tensor and measurement order, the branch map including output-wire restriction, classical basis-selection functions, and terminal correction semantics.

items.title: Adaptive J angle and Pauli-frame update
items.statement:
Let a one-qubit input carry the Pauli frame $X^xZ^z$, where $x,z\in\{0,1\}$,
and let $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Choose the next equatorial measurement angle
$(-1)^x\beta$. For outcome $b\in\{0,1\}$, the one-bit teleportation branch is

$$ 2^{-1/2}\gamma(x,z,\beta)X^{b\oplus z}Z^xJ(\beta),\qquad \gamma(x,z,\beta)=\begin{cases}1,&x=0,\\(-1)^ze^{-i\beta},&x=1.\end{cases} $$

Thus the updated Pauli frame is $(x',z')=(b\oplus z,x)$, and the exact
branch scalar has unit modulus.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: multiply the displayed matrices in the fixed J convention, track the global scalar, and verify the Pauli-frame bit update.

items.title: Normalized transport rounds preserve the circuit up to a recorded phase
items.statement:
For a circuit $C$ as in [[def-qc-normalized-transport-schedule]], let
$U_C$ be its denotation and let $\widetilde U_C$ be the chronological product
of the normalized rounds. Then

$$\widetilde U_C=\sigma_C U_C.$$

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §20.6
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, §§II D–F

proof_obligations: Check each of the four layer cases and multiply equalities in chronological order, retaining all phases.

items.title: Normalized transport encoding is a finite simple graph of bounded size
items.statement:
Let $C$ be an $n$-wire, $d$-layer circuit and let $R$ be the number of rounds
in the normalized schedule. Form a candidate vertex list
$V_T=\{v_{j,s}:1\le j\le n,\ 0\le s\le R\}$, horizontal edges
$\{v_{j,s-1},v_{j,s}\}$, and vertical edges
$\{v_{j,s-1},v_{k,s-1}\}$ for each $\{j,k\}\in M_s$. Each edge list is
loop-free and duplicate-free, the lists are disjoint, and their union is a
finite simple graph with exactly $n(R+1)$ vertices and $R\le3d$; thus the
graph object used in the Definition is well-defined.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: Check zero wires, zero layers, empty CZ layers, fully occupied J layers, mixed J/idle layers, and uniqueness of horizontal versus vertical edges.

items.title: Exact finite unitary synthesis from cosine-sine recursion
items.statement:
For every $n\ge1$ and $U\in U(2^n)$, there is a finite exact $n$-wire
circuit with no ancillas, using arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOT gates,
whose denotation is exactly $U$. For $n=0$, the unitary channel on the
one-dimensional register is the identity channel and is represented by the
empty circuit. The finite alphabet may be chosen to contain the exact gate
matrices used in the construction. This is an existence theorem for exact
mathematical gate labels; it gives no finite-bit encoding or decomposition-time
bound.

references.title: Vivek V. Shende, Stephen S. Bullock, and Igor L. Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, arXiv:quant-ph/0406176v5, §§5.1–5.3
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415, §2.2

proof_obligations: Derive the unoptimized finite QSD recursion, compile the central Ry and both diagonal Rz multiplexors exactly, and handle n=0,1,2.
Do not use the unproved optimized CNOT saving or claim finite-bit synthesis complexity.

items.title: Graph-state stabilizer generators
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an ordered finite simple graph and let $|G\rangle$ be its
graph state. Write $X_v,Z_v$ for the one-qubit Pauli matrices embedded on the
tensor factor indexed by $v$; in the phase-aware Pauli convention, vertex at
zero-based position $r$ is wire $r+1$. For $v\in V$, put
$K_v:=X_v\prod_{u\in N(v)}Z_u$. Each $K_v$ is a Hermitian involution,
$K_v|G\rangle=|G\rangle$, the generators commute pairwise, and their binary
Pauli labels are independent. This includes $V=\varnothing$, where the
generating family is empty.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: conjugate Xᵥ through incident CZ gates; adjacent generators have two local anticommutations; Kᵥ has a unique X at v.

items.title: Four-branch open-graph pattern for CZ
items.statement:
Take vertices $1,2$ as inputs and $3,4$ as outputs, with edges
$\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,4\}$. Prepare
$CZ_{12}CZ_{13}CZ_{24}(|\psi\rangle_{12}|+\rangle_3|+\rangle_4)$ and measure
vertices $1,2$ in the $J(0)=H$ basis. For outcomes $b_1,b_2\in\{0,1\}$,
the branch operator from the two input wires to the two output wires is

$$K_{b_1b_2}=\frac12(X^{b_1}H\otimes X^{b_2}H)CZ.$$

Each of the four branches has probability $1/4$ for every normalized input,
and the terminal correction $(HX^{b_1}\otimes HX^{b_2})$ yields the corrected
branch $\frac12 CZ|\psi\rangle$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: expand all four outcome branches with the declared wire order; verify each branch has probability 1/4 and its output equals the displayed corrected CZ branch.

items.title: Pattern branch probabilities and zero-probability transcripts
items.statement:
For a finite adaptive pattern with transcript branch maps $K_{\mathbf b}$, a
normalized pure input $|\psi\rangle$ has
$p_{\mathbf b}=\|K_{\mathbf b}|\psi\rangle\|^2$ and
$\sum_{\mathbf b}p_{\mathbf b}=1$. For a density operator $\rho$, the branch
probability is $p_{\mathbf b}=\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho
K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)$ and these probabilities also sum to one. A transcript
with $p_{\mathbf b}=0$ is impossible and has no normalized conditional output;
normalization is defined only for positive-probability branches.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415

proof_obligations: derive each branch map from the ordered measurement instrument and show probabilities sum to one across all adaptive transcripts.

items.title: Circuit-to-open-graph resource encoding with normalized transport rounds
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a finite J/CZ circuit and let $\mathcal T(C)$ have rounds
$(M_s,(\alpha_{s1},\ldots,\alpha_{sn}))_{s=1}^R$ and recorded scalar
$\sigma_C$ as in [[def-qc-normalized-transport-schedule]]. The schedule index
$j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ denotes source circuit wire $j-1$; thus a schedule edge
$\{j,k\}$ corresponds to the source-wire pair $\{j-1,k-1\}$. Coordinate
$j$ of every frame vector denotes this same wire. The encoded graph
$G_C$ has vertices $v_{j,s}$ for $1\le j\le n$ and $0\le s\le R$,
horizontal edges $\{v_{j,s-1},v_{j,s}\}$, and vertical edges
$\{v_{j,s-1},v_{k,s-1}\}$ for $\{j,k\}\in M_s$. It is a finite simple
graph by [[lem-qc-transport-encoding-is-simple-and-size-bounded]]. Its input
vertices are $I=\{v_{j,0}:1\le j\le n\}$, its outputs are
$O=\{v_{j,R}:1\le j\le n\}$, and its ordered vertex register follows wire
index first and then column index. In particular, the inherited orders on
$I$ and $O$ are $v_{1,0},\ldots,v_{n,0}$ and
$v_{1,R},\ldots,v_{n,R}$, matching source circuit wire order
$0,\ldots,n-1$. The pattern’s measurement order on the vertices
$v_{j,s-1}$ is round-major, wire-minor, for $s=1,\ldots,R$ and
$j=1,\ldots,n$.

The adaptive basis angles and terminal correction are defined from the
outcome blocks $b^s=(b^s_1,\ldots,b^s_n)$ as follows. Let $A_s$ be the binary
adjacency matrix of $M_s$ with vertex order $1,\ldots,n$ (vertex $j$ is
position $j-1$ in the zero-based order of [[def-qc-binary-adjacency-matrix]]),
so
$(A_s)_{jk}=1$ exactly when $\{j,k\}\in M_s$. Matrix-vector products and
all frame vectors use these coordinates; binary dot products mean
$u\cdot v=\sum_{j=1}^n u_jv_j\in\mathbb F_2$. The frame functions are defined recursively by
$x^0=z^0=0\in\mathbb F_2^n$ and the following formulas. Before round $s$, define

$$z^{s,*}:=z^{s-1}\oplus A_sx^{s-1},\qquad \theta_{sj}:=(-1)^{x^{s-1}_j}\alpha_{sj}.$$

For an outcome block $b^s$, the post-round frame is defined by
$x^s:=b^s\oplus z^{s,*}$ and $z^s:=x^{s-1}$. The function of earlier
outcomes given by these recurrences selects the equatorial measurement basis
at each vertex. For a complete transcript $\mathbf b$, the
terminal frame and correction are the following functions. For $n\ge1$, the zero-scalar Pauli frame is
$P(x,z):=X^xZ^z=P(0,x,z)$ from
[[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]], and the terminal correction is
$C(\mathbf b):=P(x^R,z^R)^\dagger$. For $n=0$, the empty frame is
$P((),()):=I_{\mathbb C}$ and the correction is the identity on the
one-dimensional register.

For $n\ge1$, define
$\gamma(x,z,\alpha)=1$ if $x=0$ and
$\gamma(x,z,\alpha)=(-1)^ze^{-i\alpha}$ if $x=1$, as in
[[lem-qc-adaptive-angle-pauli-frame-update]], and put

$$\lambda_{\mathbf b}:=\sigma_C\prod_{s=1}^R\left[ (-1)^{\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M_s}x^{s-1}_jx^{s-1}_k} \prod_{j=1}^n\gamma(x^{s-1}_j,z^{s,*}_j,\alpha_{sj})\right].$$

For $n=0$, the empty transcript has scalar $\lambda=1$. The encoding
retains these exact scalars; no global phase is discarded. Its graph has
$n(R+1)$ vertices and $R\le3d$ for $d$ original layers. The item
[[lem-qc-normalized-rounds-preserve-circuit]] proves that the normalized
round circuit is $\sigma_C U_C$; the branch theorem proves the resulting
pattern's relation to $U_C$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: specify schedule and show no duplicated edges.

items.title: Every finite open-graph pattern is a measurement circuit
items.statement:
Every finite open-graph adaptive pattern has a finite **raw measurement circuit** that preserves its arbitrary input, adjoins $|+\rangle$ ancillas on $V\setminus I$, applies one $CZ$ per graph edge, performs the same ordered projective measurements with the same transcript-dependent bases, and retains the same ordered output wires. Its branch operator on transcript $\mathbf b$ is exactly the pattern's raw operator $K_{\mathbf b}$, including its scalar phase. Thus for every density input $\rho$ both have branch probability
$$p_{\mathbf b}=\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^*),$$
and, when $p_{\mathbf b}>0$, the same raw conditional output $\rho_{\mathbf b}=K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^*/p_{\mathbf b}$.

Appending the pattern's specified transcript-controlled suffix $C(\mathbf b)$ gives a **corrected measurement circuit** with branch operator $L_{\mathbf b}=C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$. This equals the corrected pattern branch operator, has the same probability $p_{\mathbf b}$, and has conditional output $C(\mathbf b)\rho_{\mathbf b}C(\mathbf b)^*$ whenever $p_{\mathbf b}>0$. Both raw presentations have the same transcript-labelled instrument, and both corrected presentations have the same corrected transcript-labelled instrument and the same channel after forgetting the transcript. Zero-probability branches have no normalized conditional output in either presentation.

The raw circuit uses $|V|$ qubit wires, $|E|$ controlled-phase gate occurrences, and $q$ measurement occurrences under [[def-qc-adaptive-measurement-pattern]]; wire and gate counts use [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. Corrections are charged separately: the operation model must grant and cost each specified suffix call, or supply a finite construction and charge all its gate occurrences and any extra workspace. These suffix costs are added to the raw resource coordinates; they are not included in $|E|$ or supplied for free. The family of suffixes is finite because $\{0,1\}^q$ is finite. No finite-bit encoding or efficient synthesis claim for exact angles or suffix matrices is made.

references.title: Robert Raussendorf and Hans J. Briegel, Quantum computing via measurements only, arXiv:quant-ph/0010033, pp. 2–4
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, §II D, pp. 8–10

proof_obligations: preserve each branch operator and transcript probability.

items.title: A finite J/CZ circuit is simulated branch by branch by its adaptive pattern
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a finite $n$-wire J/CZ circuit with $d$ chronological layers, let
$R$ be the normalized transport-round count, and let $U_C$ be its denotation.
For the adaptive graph pattern of
[[def-qc-circuit-to-graph-resource-encoding]], every transcript
$\mathbf b\in\{0,1\}^{nR}$ has branch map

$$K_{\mathbf b}=2^{-nR/2}\lambda_{\mathbf b}P_{\mathbf b}U_C,$$

where for $n\ge1$, $P_{\mathbf b}=P(x^R,z^R)$ in the phase-aware convention,
and for $n=0$ the empty-frame convention is $P_{\mathbf b}=I_{\mathbb C}$.
The exact unit-modulus scalar $\lambda_{\mathbf b}$ is the one defined in
that encoding, including the
mixed-layer padding phase and the CZ-matching signs. Each transcript has
probability $2^{-nR}$ on every normalized pure or mixed input. Applying the
terminal correction $P_{\mathbf b}^{\dagger}$ gives the circuit output ray
on pure inputs, and summing the corrected branches gives exactly the channel
$\rho\mapsto U_C\rho U_C^{\dagger}$ on density operators. The empty-register
and zero-round cases use their unique empty transcript.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: For each transport round the arbitrary-input one-bit branch identity applies to every wire after the current CZ matching. Output Pauli frames propagate through CZ: X_c picks up Z_t and X_t picks up Z_c; commute them into the next equatorial measurement, flipping its angle and outcome bit as appropriate.

Maintain the exact branch scalar, frame, and norm invariant by induction over R rounds. Every transport contributes a fair bit; after final frame correction the output channel is the prescribed circuit, including reference correlations. Count the added identity transports; do not claim one graph column per unnormalized CZ-only layer.

items.title: Circuit and pattern translations are branch preserving and universal
items.statement:
Every finite J/CZ circuit has an adaptive open-graph pattern whose corrected
branches implement the same unitary channel and whose transcript branches
preserve the exact probabilities. Conversely, every finite open-graph
pattern has a raw measurement-circuit presentation with exactly its raw branch operators $K_{\mathbf b}$, probabilities, and positive-probability conditional outputs. Appending its specified and separately charged correction suffixes gives a corrected measurement-circuit presentation with exactly its corrected branch operators $C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$, unchanged probabilities, and corrected conditional outputs $C(\mathbf b)\rho_{\mathbf b}C(\mathbf b)^*$. The corresponding raw instruments agree transcript by transcript, as do the corresponding corrected instruments; the corrected channels agree after forgetting the transcript. For every $n\ge0$, each unitary channel on the
ordered $n$-qubit register $\mathcal Q_n$ has a J/CZ circuit representative
and hence an adaptive pattern implementing the same channel; for $n\ge1$ the
unitary matrix has size $2^n$, and for $n=0$ the channel is the identity on
$\mathbb C$. Global scalar phases are retained in branch maps and do not alter
the induced channel.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415
Robert Raussendorf and Hans J. Briegel, Quantum computing via measurements only, arXiv:quant-ph/0010033
Robert Raussendorf, Daniel E. Browne, and Hans J. Briegel, Measurement-based quantum computation on cluster states, arXiv:quant-ph/0301052

proof_obligations: combine the branch-map inductions in both directions; cite the exact QC11 synthesis theorem, derive CNOT=(I⊗H)CZ(I⊗H), use the J(α) Euler decomposition, and track transcript probabilities and output corrections.

items.title: Graph state is the unique joint stabilizer ray
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an ordered finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, let
$|G\rangle$ be its graph state, and let $K_v=X_v\prod_{u\in N(v)}Z_u$ be
the generators from [[lem-qc-graph-state-stabilizer-generators]]. Their common
$+1$ eigenspace is exactly $\operatorname{span}\{|G\rangle\}$. If $S_G$ is
the subgroup they generate, its orthogonal projector is

$$\Pi_G=2^{-n}\sum_{g\in S_G}g=|G\rangle\langle G|.$$

For $V=\varnothing$, $S_G=\{I\}$ and the formula is the identity projector
on the one-dimensional trivial register.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in graph states and its applications, arXiv:quant-ph/0602096

proof_obligations: establish full rank and apply the rank-one projector result.

title: Graph States and Measurement-Based Computation — Examples

items.title: One-edge graph state and two-wire CZ pattern
items.statement:
For the graph with vertices $1,2$ and one edge $\{1,2\}$,

$$|G\rangle=CZ|++\rangle=\tfrac12(|00\rangle+|01\rangle+|10\rangle-|11\rangle).$$

Its two graph-state generators are $K_1=X\otimes Z$ and
$K_2=Z\otimes X$. Separately, the four-vertex pattern with inputs $1,2$,
outputs $3,4$, and edges $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,4\}$ has branch
$\tfrac12(X^{b_1}H\otimes X^{b_2}H)CZ$ and terminal correction
$HX^{b_1}\otimes HX^{b_2}$. In particular, on input $|00\rangle$ all four
uncorrected outputs are $\tfrac12|++\rangle$, each with probability $1/4$,
and all corrected outputs are $\tfrac12|00\rangle$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415

proof_obligations: Verify the amplitude signs, generator products, and branch-map correction convention.
